transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but I've been having this, um, this habit with my eating lately. After my evening class, I sometimes stop for food on the way home, and I just... I end up eating a little more than I probably should. 

I'll get a full fast-food meal, and then maybe grab some candy from the vending machine, and... then I get home and have even more snacks. It's almost like I'm making up for the whole day, if that makes sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay. I know it's probably just a silly habit, but I wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by coming in to talk about it. Does that... does that help answer your question?

When you say you eat more than you probably should, would you say you're eating an unusually large amount of food in one sitting, like a whole large pizza or multiple fast-food meals, in a short period of time?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's like a whole large pizza or anything quite that extreme. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, you know? 

It's more like... like I mentioned, I'll get that full fast-food meal on the way home, and then the candy, and then... yeah, I'll have a few more snacks once I'm actually in the house. It just sort of adds up over the course of the evening. It feels like a lot to me, like I'm eating for the whole day right then and there. But maybe it's not as unusual as I'm making it out to be? I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely out of control. Does that make sense, Doctor? Am I explaining it right?

So you mentioned that you eat a fast-food meal, candy, and then more snacks in the evening. Would you say that during this time you eat much more quickly than usual or until you feel uncomfortably full?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't really say that. I don't think I'm rushing through it or eating super fast or anything. I usually just try to take my time, maybe while I'm catching up on a little paperwork from the office or watching TV. 

And I definitely try not to eat until I'm... you know, uncomfortably stuffed or sick. I just like to feel satisfied after a long day of looking at numbers, I guess. I try to be reasonable about it, so I haven't really noticed feeling overly full like that. I hope that's alright? I mean, I'm trying to give you the best picture I can. Is that the kind of information you were looking for, Doctor?
During these evenings when you're eating more than you think you should, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating or that you're losing control over how much you eat?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I wouldn't say I completely lose control, like I'm totally out of my mind or anything. I'm always aware of what I'm doing. 

But, well, sometimes... once I start on those snacks, I do keep telling myself, you know, just close the bag, put it away, and go to bed. But... it's like my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. And then I end up feeling really embarrassed, just kind of sick of myself for not stopping when I said I would. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible. I really try to be disciplined, I promise. It's just... those evenings can be a little tough. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... is that helpful for you to know?
After these evenings of eating more than you'd like, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Oh... um... well... I definitely don't use laxatives or anything like that. And I'm not exactly running miles and miles at my age. But... well, I'm really embarrassed to admit this, Doctor. Please don't think badly of me, but... a few times... just a handful of times after those late-night eating spells, I... I have gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up. 

I just got so scared that all that extra food would show on me, you know? Sitting at a desk doing the books all day, it's so easy to put on weight, and I just panicked. But it's really not a regular thing, I promise. I try very hard to keep things under control so it doesn't get to that point. 

I hope you can understand... I know it's not a good thing to do, but I'm just trying to be completely honest with you. Is it okay that I shared that? I really hope you don't think less of me.
How often have you made yourself vomit after those late-night eating episodes?

Oh, um... well... I guess if I really think about it... for about the past three months or so, it's been... maybe just once a week? Usually on a night when I've had a particularly stressful day with the accounts, or... well, I actually take a little evening class right now, just a continuing education thing, and sometimes after that I'll have one of those nights where I eat too much and then... you know, make myself sick. 

But it's really just that one night a week, I swear. I try so hard the rest of the time to be good and keep everything balanced. I know even once a week isn't great, and I'm really trying to stop... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. Does that sound like the kind of detail you need, Doctor? I really hope I'm being helpful.
Can you tell me if the times when you eat more than you'd like tend to happen in specific, short periods—like within a couple of hours—or does it feel more spread out over the whole evening?

Well, um... I suppose it's mostly in a pretty short window. Like within just a couple of hours. Usually, it happens right after that evening class I mentioned. I'll... well, I sometimes stop for food on the way back and get a full fast-food meal. And then, I might grab some candy from the vending machine, and... by the time I get home, I end up having even more snacks. 

It's almost like I'm trying to make up for the whole day, just all at once. I know it probably sounds like an awful lot of food when I list it out like that... I'm really a bit ashamed to admit it. I really don't mean to let it get out of hand, I try to be good during the day. Does that answer your question, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the way you need me to.
When you're eating more than you'd like, does it feel like it happens all at once in a short, specific episode, or is it more like you graze on food off and on throughout the evening?

Well, um... I guess I might have repeated myself a little there, I'm sorry. But yes, it's definitely more of a... a specific episode, I suppose you could call it. It's not really grazing all night. 

Like I was saying, it's usually right after my evening class. I'll just... I'll stop and get a full fast-food meal, and then maybe grab some candy from the vending machine, and then I get home and just keep having more snacks. It all happens pretty fast, really, like I'm just trying to make up for not eating much during the day. It's all kind of bunched together. 

I hope I'm making sense. I know it's a lot of food to eat all at once, and I really am trying to do better... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the clear picture you need. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for?

Do these episodes of eating more than you'd like cause you a lot of distress, or do they ever interfere with your daily life, like making you late for work, avoiding social events, or feeling ashamed to eat around others?

Oh, um... well, it definitely causes me some distress. I mean, I feel awful about it. But I don't let it ruin my life or anything! I still get all my bookkeeping work done, and I'm keeping up with my coursework just fine. I'm very responsible about my job. 

I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest... I have started sort of... slipping out of class a little quickly when it's over. Some of the other folks will hang around to chat, and I just... I kind of avoid that casual time now. I think I just feel so ashamed of what I'm about to go do, and I get a bit preoccupied with just getting home so I can... you know. 

But I'm still functioning perfectly well at work, I promise. I don't let it affect my professional life. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope it doesn't make me sound too terrible... I really am trying to keep everything on track.
During these episodes when you're eating more than you'd like, would you say that you feel like you can't stop eating or that you're losing control over how much you're eating?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I wouldn't say I completely lose control, exactly. I always know what I'm doing. But... well, it is a little hard to stop once I get going. 

Like, once I start on those snacks after I get home, I'll... I keep telling myself, you know, just close the bag, put it away, go to bed. I know I should. But... my hands just sort of keep reaching for more. And before I know it, I've had way more than I meant to, and I just feel so embarrassed... and honestly, a bit sick of myself for not just stopping when I told myself to. 

But I am trying to be better about it, I really am! I know it's just a matter of willpower. Does that sound like what you were asking, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

Can you tell me if, during these episodes, you feel like you've crossed a threshold where you just can't stop eating, even though you want to, or if it's more like you choose to keep eating but wish you didn't?

Well, um... I guess... I might be repeating myself a little bit here, and I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it right. But, um... it's kind of like... well, I know I *should* choose to stop. 

Like I was saying about the snacks when I get home... I'll be sitting there, and in my head, I'm telling myself, "Okay, that's enough, just close the bag, put it away, and go to bed." But then... it's like my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. It's not that I don't know what I'm doing, it's just... I can't seem to make myself stop in that moment, even though I want to. And then afterward, I just feel so embarrassed and, well, sick of myself for letting it happen again. 

I don't want you to think I'm completely out of control or anything, I'm really not! It's just those specific moments where it gets a little away from me. Does that answer your question, Doctor? I hope I'm being helpful.

During these episodes, would you say that you feel like you’ve crossed a point where you just can’t stop eating, even though you want to, or does it feel more like you’re choosing to keep eating even though you wish you didn’t?

Oh, um... well, I know you just asked me that, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you a clear enough answer. I really don't mean to be difficult or make you repeat yourself! 

I guess... well, I wouldn't say I've crossed a point where I absolutely *can't* stop. That sounds so... severe, you know? Like I've completely lost my mind or something. And I'm really a very put-together person, I promise. 

It's more just... a struggle in the moment. I know I *could* choose to stop, and I *want* to choose to stop, but I just... don't. Or I can't quite find the willpower right then. So maybe it is more like choosing to keep eating, even though I'm wishing the whole time that I wasn't doing it. 

I hope that makes more sense? I'm really trying to explain it right for you, Doctor. I just don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is.
During these episodes, would you say that you feel like you’ve crossed a point where you just can’t stop eating, even though you want to?

Oh, dear... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm making you ask the exact same thing over and over. I must be doing a terrible job of explaining myself, and I really apologize for taking up your time like this. 

Um... if I have to put it simply... yes, I suppose it is like I cross a point where I just can't stop. Like I said before, once I start on those snacks after work, I'm sitting there telling myself, over and over, "Just close the bag, put it away, go to bed." But... my hands just keep reaching for more, almost like they have a mind of their own. And I just keep going until I feel so embarrassed and sick of myself. 

I know it sounds awful when I say it out loud like that. I really am a very disciplined person in every other part of my life, especially at work with my accounting—I'm very precise! It's just this one little thing that gets away from me. Does that finally answer what you were looking for, Doctor? I really hope I'm giving you the right information now.
